(the holy hour each sunday evening in st mary’s oratory will cease for the moment, resuming after christmas.) “november remember ” pastoral initiative with the grim statistic of there having been 150 people killed on the country’s roads so far this year (12 more than the same period last year) – 45 of these people aged under 25 and 30 aged over 65 (of the 29 pedestrians killed, 10 were over 65) – we need to redouble our efforts as road users to do what we can to make our roads safer, especially as we enter the darker and colder months. to this end, while november is a time when we remember our dead, this year, in an att empt to acknowledge that the life and death of each of us has its influence on others, we would like as many people as possible to take on a pledge to use the roads with care in november. the de tails of that pledge are to be found on posters and our social media pages. also, next weekend, people ar asked to collect a prayer card for their car to be recited each day during the mo nth and a bottle of holy water to be sprinkled on their car and kept there. chief superintendent goretti sheridan will address the cockhill novena on sunday 1 nove mber and launch this initiative. there will be signage placed on the roads entering our two pari shes to remind us of this. please do your best to participate in this and support it. father bradley acknowledgement of
